Purpose: Primary-source observations supporting investigation and enrichment. These are not claims of missing Microsoft detections or proof of tenant telemetry availability.

Reports.Title: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing
Reports.Attribution: Storm-2992 develops/supports EvilTokens; do not attribute all customer intrusions to that actor.
Reports.Observed: Device-code phishing, Microsoft Graph organizational discovery, compromised mailbox review, and in an observed incident email exfiltration and inbox-rule persistence; financial-authority users were targeted.
Reports.Visibility: Supported cloud workload audit events and app metadata; authentication/token and detailed Graph activity require their respective telemetry. Not every Graph request is a CloudAppEvents row.
Reports.NativeOverlap: Report lists device-code authentication, anomalous Graph activity after device-code phishing, and suspicious inbox-rule creation after device-code phishing detections.
Reports.Enhancement: Protected business-resource and identity context; watched-app timelines. Protected-resource policy rule is a design inference, not a campaign-identifying signature.

Reports.Title: Impersonating IT support: Threat actors turn remote session into enterprise-wide access
Reports.Observed: External Teams contact impersonating IT support, a legitimate remote-support session, malicious MSI/Node.js implants, AD reconnaissance and WinRM toward domain controllers/certificate authorities.
Reports.Visibility: Teams audit/alert evidence where supported; endpoint execution and identity pivots require MDE/identity telemetry. Cloud Apps alone cannot establish this entire chain.
Reports.NativeOverlap: Report lists native suspicious external Teams chat, IT-support voice phishing and related dangerous-command alerts, plus endpoint/identity detections. Alert titles are illustrative and may vary.
Reports.Enhancement: Bounded same-Entra-user alert-to-endpoint correlation. Uses alert creation time, not contact time; it does not detect or prove a remote session or Tier-0 pivot.

Reports.Title: Email threat landscape: Q2 2026 trends and insights
Reports.Attribution: Unnamed actors for the relevant OAuth-redirect and Teams examples; do not transfer attribution from other sections.
Reports.Observed: June 15 OAuth error/redirect flow abuse involving an attacker-registered multitenant app delivered a batch-file malware payload. Teams impersonation also used generic and SaaS/update-themed identities.
Reports.Visibility: Teams activity where collected. External app registration/redirect configuration is not necessarily present in the victim tenant; URL and endpoint evidence are needed for the delivery chain.
Reports.NativeOverlap: Email/URL and endpoint detections are documented. No campaign-specific Cloud Apps detection was established by this research.
Reports.Enhancement: Context for Teams hunting. OAuth redirect delivery remains a manual cross-product investigation lead, not a shipped detection or a claim of consent/token theft.

Reports.Title: Breaking the code: Multi-stage code of conduct phishing campaign leads to AiTM token compromise
Reports.Observed: Compliance-themed phishing through PDFs, CAPTCHA/staging pages and adversary-in-the-middle authentication capturing tokens.
Reports.Visibility: Subsequent supported cloud activity and existing anomaly alerts. Token-risk and sign-in evidence require appropriate Entra telemetry.
Reports.NativeOverlap: Report explicitly lists Cloud Apps impossible travel and Entra anomalous-token/unfamiliar-sign-in detections.
Reports.Enhancement: Protected-account alert context and subsequent resource-access hunting. Downstream mailbox/Graph collection is not established by this report.

Reports.Title: Email threat landscape: Q3 2026 trends and insights
Reports.Attribution: Unnamed actors for the relevant device-code and Teams examples.
Reports.Observed: Salary-review lures used branded documents, QR codes, fake OneDrive pages and device-code authentication. Malicious Teams call attempts increasingly used ordinary personal names.
Reports.Visibility: Supported subsequent cloud activity and Teams evidence. Device-code authentication requires identity telemetry; no campaign-specific Cloud Apps rule was verified.
Reports.NativeOverlap: Report lists email/URL and endpoint protections; do not infer a Cloud Apps gap from an absent rule listing.
Reports.Enhancement: Do not rely solely on helpdesk-themed names. Use reviewed native alerts and entity-linked endpoint context. Attempted calls are not successful contact; the described token-transfer mechanism is not proof every target completed sign-in.
